# Beyond Simple A/B Tests {.unnumbered}

*A Practical Guide to Modern Experimentation*

This book is a practical guide to modern A/B testing.

It starts from the basic structure of a clean experiment, then moves into the problems that appear in real product systems: ratio metrics, peeking, variance reduction, multiple testing, noncompliance, interference, concurrent experiments, heterogeneous treatment effects, long-term holdouts, and adaptive experiments.

The goal is not only to explain statistical methods. The goal is to build product judgment: how to translate a business question into an experiment, how to choose metrics, how to detect when a result is misleading, and how to make a decision when the data is useful but imperfect.

## How to Read This Book

The chapters are arranged in five parts.

### Part I: Foundations

The first part explains what an experiment is really testing. It covers hypotheses, treatment effects, randomization, sample size, duration, and metric design.

### Part II: Inference Problems

The second part focuses on statistical problems that often appear even when the experiment itself is randomized: peeking, variance reduction, and multiple testing.

### Part III: Real-World Experiment Complications

The third part discusses issues that appear in production systems: triggered analysis, noncompliance, interference, network effects, and overlapping experiments.

### Part IV: Learning Beyond the Average

The fourth part moves beyond the average treatment effect. It covers heterogeneous effects, long-term effects, holdouts, and adaptive experiments.

### Part V: When Randomization Is Hard

The final part is planned for later chapters. It will cover quasi-experiments, experiment quality checks, and launch decisions.
